general_information.Description: This course provides an introduction to aesthetic and the phylosophy of arts for students and provides them with the knowledge and skills to communicate their ideas and processes in a visual form more effectively. As a means of questioning and applying fundamental theories, concepts and techniques, students conduct research and produce practical projects. The course examines the basic elements of visual communication and how context shapes visual forms production and reception.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 2. Actively participate in class activities 3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 5. Read the textbook in advance 6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: (Basic Knowledge) Understand the way people thinking about Arts - Aesthetics.

(Research Skills) Understand the contexts of the main styles and movements in Art History, which related to important inventions in manufacture, significant events on the market, talented and pioneering Artist.
(Critical Thinking) Analyze the records of the past in Art and Phylosophy History.
(Communication Skills): Study optional cases in aesthetic history, organize and express the individual thoughts clearly and coherently both in orally (presentations) and writing (assignments/essays).
Be aware of what is aesthetics and understand the stages of aesthetic awareness in history
Evaluate manual and/or digital art works, media and materials appropriately to produce creative ways solutions for specific cultural and technical contexts.
Having a professional style in arts activity. Love to research in visual arts.
Students have a proficient in presentation and teamworks.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1.1
constructive_questions.Details: Who discussed beauty in the ancient period?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.1
constructive_questions.Details: Who discussed beauty in the medieval period?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.1
constructive_questions.Details: Who discussed aesthetics in the modern period?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4.1
constructive_questions.Details: "What is Art? If our current concept of art did not arise until the eighteenth century, is it unacceptably anachronistic to apply our term to pre-eighteenth- century ‘art’? Is it reasonable to use a work like the Mona Lisa (1503) to test our current definitions?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ5.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is "Art as representation"? Art as form ?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is "Art as expression" ? What is the Art and aesthetic function ?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.1
constructive_questions.Details: Is ‘art’ something that needs to be defined? What happens if we are unable to settle on such a definition? Should a definition of art be expected to tell us anything about how art should be interpreted or evaluated? Why or why not?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is "On interpretation"?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.2
constructive_questions.Details: Why did identifying correct, reasonable, or meaningful interpretations of art become important during the Romantic period?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.3
constructive_questions.Details: According to the group's point of view, how should the meaning of the work originate from the author's intention be viewed?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.1
constructive_questions.Details: Some anti-intentionalists, like Wimsatt and Beardsley, have argued that meaning is determined centrally by what is in the text, what do you think about this?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.2
constructive_questions.Details: It should be noted that although discussion in this chapter has centred primarily on literary works, much of what is said here applies to other sorts of artworks as well. What do you think about this?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.3
constructive_questions.Details: Should different types of art be evaluated differently and what criteria are needed?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10.1
constructive_questions.Details: Read the case study in the textbook and discuss about the challenges of making judgments about a work based on the viewer's perspective?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10.2
constructive_questions.Details: What is Hypothetical intentionalists?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10.3
constructive_questions.Details: Gaut Interpreting the Arts: Gaut has suggested that each view has its merits and drawbacks, and that each perspective has a role to play in interpreting art. What do you think about this?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11.1
constructive_questions.Details: In general, since Pythagoras’s time, what we have seen are attempts to ground beauty, aesthetic properties and the value of art in something determinable so that we have at least some basis for disagreements about particular cases of art and beauty. Do you agree with this point of view and why?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11.2
constructive_questions.Details: After the Romantic period were there more theories about how to interpret a work of art? Provide evidence and analysis?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11.3
constructive_questions.Details: Who are the intentionalist arguments mentioned in this chapter?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ13.1
constructive_questions.Details: Does beauty have an objective nature? Is taste simply subjective? Is there a right way to experience art?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ14.1
constructive_questions.Details: What sorts of properties are aesthetic properties, and what do they depend on? The view that a work of art does not need to have any value but only needs to be beautiful or satisfy the viewer's emotions, what aestheticist's view does it remind of and how do you evaluate this view?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ15.1
constructive_questions.Details: Does art have a unique sort of value – and if so, what kind of value is it? What all of these philosophers would seem to agree about is that artistic value is ultimately grounded – one way or another – in aesthetic value? Do you agree with this point of view? Please explain the yes or no answer using the works in this chapter? In general, since Pythagoras’s time, what we have seen are attempts to ground beauty, aesthetic properties and the value of art in something determinable so that we have at least some basis for disagreements about particular cases of art and beauty. Has this view changed much to this day?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is the Ontology of Art?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16.2
constructive_questions.Details: What is the physical objects hypothesis ?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17.1
constructive_questions.Details: How to identify singular and multiple artworks in other arts types?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17.2
constructive_questions.Details: How differrence betwween Alabama Tenant Farmer Wife (1936) and After Walker Evans: 4 (1981)?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ18.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is the structuralist view of the ontology of art?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is tragedy ?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19.2
constructive_questions.Details: What is the emotion in art?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ20.1
constructive_questions.Details: A work of art is a mental object. How do you think about that opinion?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ21.1
constructive_questions.Details: Did Ancient philosophers address the issue of "ethics in art"? If so, what are their views?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ21.2
constructive_questions.Details: How are ethical issues in art perceived by modern authors?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ22.1
constructive_questions.Details: What are the concept of "beauty" and "good"?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ22.2
constructive_questions.Details: What is the relationship between Aesthetics and Ethics? What is aesthetics? What criteria to evaluate Aesthetics? What is ethics? What are the criteria to evaluate morality?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ23.1
constructive_questions.Details: How do Ethics - Aesthetics and Art interact with each other? Can ethics be considered a criterion for evaluating Aesthetics? Can morality be considered a criterion for evaluating Art?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ23.2
constructive_questions.Details: What does Marco Evaristti's Helena (2000) reflect? In your opinion, should there be censorship of art?

constructive_questions.Details: Is there racism in art
What do you think about: Western actors playing Asian characters, white actors playing black characters
